blockers: Need order-swapped pairwise votes from at least three genuinely distinct model families and providers.

Need usable train labels across at least three training repositories plus repository-held-out development observations; both the cross-repository and adaptive label-seeking pairs had unchanged outcomes and create no new labels.
Need a repository-held-out candidate profile trained without safety-gate leakage.
Need paired real-agent frozen-baseline/candidate shadow runs bound to that profile.
Need at least 50 sealed tasks across three repositories, ten sequences, and two unseen agent models with complete paired cost data.
Need a passing explicit promotion decision before any atomic activation can be considered.

limitations: All reviewer roles came from one Codex model family.
The judgments are pointwise rubric labels, not order-swapped pairwise comparisons.
Relevance agreement was weak after chance correction, so this remains diagnostic only.
The runtime is a deterministic fixture rather than a coding model.
The run covers one task and three retrieval conditions, not a selected-memory ablation.
Its declared effect claim is none.
The two pairs cover one SWE-bench Verified task, one repository, and one coding-agent model.
One discordant pair produced a real TRAIN label; this summary is not itself a training JSONL input.
Provider cost was unavailable, and no candidate profile or promotion claim is made.
The three valid pairs cover one task each from Pylint, pytest, and Seaborn with one coding-agent model.
All three pairs had unchanged executable outcomes and therefore create no causal training labels.
Invalid scorer-development attempts are explicitly hash-bound and excluded from the aggregate.
The four valid adaptively selected pairs cover three registered tasks from Pylint and pytest with one coding-agent model; they are not a product-effect sample.
All four valid pairs had unchanged executable outcomes and therefore create no causal training labels.
The two bound post-run audits exclude three scorer-invalid V1 pairs and one V2 agent-protocol violation from every count.
